result.title: Commit or Abstain? System One Decision Models, LLMs, and Missing Legal Authority
result.comment: 16 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables. Under review. Code, data, and model outputs: https://github.com/mmikaildemir/commit-or-abstain
result.summary: Given the enormous number of claims to be checked, verifiable legal AI requires scalable, cost-effective models that answer the practical needs of law. System One decision models are built on large language models but, instead of generating text, return a calibrated probability for each option. This suits the verification of legal authority, where the question is closed: a given holding, or none of them. We test whether such models abstain when the correct authority is missing. We extend CaseHOLD with an abstention condition in which the correct holding is replaced in 1,670 of 5,314 items, and compare four decision models with six generative LLMs. When no option is correct, generative LLMs still pick one in 38-86% of items; the most cautious decision model does so in 30%. On standard CaseHOLD, a decision model matches the best generative LLM (88.1% vs. 88.2%) at 1/55 of the cost. Accepting that LLM's answer only when a decision model agrees halves its wrong citations, and distilling a decision model's probabilities into Qwen3-8B, without labels, yields a well-calibrated local model. Legal AI should be judged by its wrong citations, not by accuracy alone.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 CaseHOLD 上加入弃答条件（5,314 项中 1,670 项替换掉正确 holding），比较四个「只输出各选项校准概率」的决策模型与六个生成式 LLM 在缺少正确权威时是否弃答，并报告标准集上的成本效率与无标签概率蒸馏结果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以校准概率作为独立决策头、在证据缺失时触发弃答，以及靠与决策模型的一致性门控将错误引用减半，可为 LVR 的「STOP／验证」判据与证据不足时的拒答提供核查线索；但属纯文本法律场景，未涉及视觉或 latent 推理状态。
